title: Quickfire reliability standup notes + action plan
content:
Purpose / context:
- Prep notes for weekly SRE ops sync (30 min). Quick snapshot to run during standup then expand in followups.
- Focus areas: SLO health, paging trends, top 3 incidents, mitigation progress, short action list for next week.

Agenda (30m):
- 0-3m: quick SLO snapshot + urgency flags (me)
- 3-10m: paging trend highlights (Samir)
- 10-18m: incident rollup (Nina) — root cause + current mitigation state
- 18-25m: blockers & owner assignment (all)
- 25-30m: quick wins / runbook gaps to capture (me)

Quick SLO snapshot (to paste into meeting):
- External API latency SLO: 99p < 200ms. Current 7d rolling: 99p = 238ms (+19% vs baseline). Error budget burn: 4.2% per day (7d avg) — projection: budget exhausted in ~18 days if trend continues.
- Inference availability SLO: 99.9% (monthly). March rolling: 99.87% (minor deficit). Main contributors: cold-start throttles and autoscaler flaps.
- Embeddings throughput SLO: 95p throughput target met, but tail latencies show spikes during model rollovers.

Immediate flags (call these out early):
- Latency 99p breach risk for API calls — need to reduce tail (kv cache warming / batching policy adjustments).
- Oncall reports increasing pages for "model oom" by 3x week-over-week (see Pager heatmap).

Paging trends (Samir takeaways):
- Last 7 days: 12 pager events (oncall pages), 30-day: 38. Week-on-week +42%.
- Top page categories: model-oom (45%), autoscaler-502s (25%), disk-pressure (15%), misc infra (10%), monitoring false-positive (5%).
- Time-of-day: spikes at 02:00-04:00 UTC tied to nightly batch traffic + lower capacity autoscaler thresholds.
- Hypothesis: a recent scheduler change (k8s eviction window) + slightly reduced headroom on dedicated pools increased OOMs.

Top incidents (candidate roll-up for meeting):
- INC-SRE-2026-031 (Mar 22): model-batch-failure -> root cause: batch collider in runtime kernel after change in attention kernel selection; mitigation: rollback kernel-selection flag (deployed), hotfix to batch size limiter (PR merged, canary + tomorrow full). Postmortem in progress (SRE-4321).
- INC-SRE-2026-038 (Mar 27): autoscaler 502s during rapid traffic spike -> root cause: incorrect healthprobe threshold + burst scaling race; mitigation: increased probe window and added short warm pool for spikes; follow-up: autoscaler e2e test (SRE-4377).
- INC-SRE-2026-044 (Apr 1): disk-pressure on serv-2 -> root cause: log-rotate backlog + monitoring agent IO pattern; mitigation: log-rotate tuning and limit agent FS read frequency.

Runbook / knowledge gaps spotted:
- No clear documented checklist for "model OOM page" that lists immediate throttles to enable and who to loop in (ML infra vs runtime). NEED: 10-step runbook draft.
- Autoscaler playbook exists but lacks a quick test to simulate burst traffic in staging. NEED: small harness + one pager.
- Postmortem templates inconsistent: some include impact timeline, others don't — standardize to include token-level cost estimate and customer-facing impact blurb.

Quick tactical suggestions (to propose in meeting):
- Short term (1-3 days):
  - Lower default batch-size cap for certain models — quick config change, ~1h deploy, owner: Nina.
  - Add a temporary prefix-KV caching enable for 2 high-traffic routes to cut tail latency — owner: me (Erin), risk: small memory bump on serving nodes.
  - Increase autoscaler probe window and add 10% buffer to dedicated pool headroom — owner: Samir, depends on capacity budget.
- Medium term (1-3 weeks):
  - Implement autoscaler e2e test that replays spike trace and validates zero 502s (ticket SRE-4377). Owner: infra-test eng.
  - Create runbook for model-oom pages + tabletop drill in next oncall cycle. Owner: ops-lead.

Action items (assignable lines):
- Erin: Draft model-oom 10-step runbook (target: EOD Wed) — include immediate throttles, rollback steps, Slack escalation channel, and who to call for kernel rollbacks.
- Samir: Run quick capacity audit on dedicated pools and propose +10% buffer where safe (target: 3 days). Add autoscaler probe change PR and coordinate with release-engineering.
- Nina: Deploy batch-size cap change in canary and monitor 99p latency delta (target: canary in 24h). File follow-up with perf numbers.
- Ops-team: Schedule a short tabletop for model-oom on next oncall rotation (owner: ops-lead).
- SRE Docs owner: Consolidate postmortem template into Confluence and include cost-impact section (target: 2 weeks).

Notes to self / talking points:
- Emphasize non-blame language; focus on systemic causes (kernel-selection heuristics + autoscaler thresholds).
- Show the quick projection chart: current 4.2%/day burn -> budget gone in ~18 days; tie to upcoming product release (release schedule next month).
- Ask product about traffic forecast for next 30 days — if growth expected, talk about pre-scaling or reserving extra capacity.

Data checks / queries to run before sync (put in chat):
- Pull 99p latency trend for last 14 days: metric query: telemetry.api.latency.p99{env:prod}.rollup(1h)
- Pager breakdown by category last 30 days: query onpagings.logs.category.count(last30d)
- Error budget burn projection script: scripts/eburn/proj.py --window 7d

Follow-up / meeting output we want:
- Agreement on 3 tactical items to execute this week (who + ETA).
- Commitment to run a tabletop for model OOM in next oncall rotation.
- Owner for autoscaler e2e test and a follow-up ticket created during meeting.

Misc scratch thoughts (not for meeting unless asked):
- Could we have a lightweight local model pool that accepts cold starts and warms KV cache without touching production serving nodes? Prototype idea — might help with cold-start tail.
- Consider adding per-route batching policies in routing layer so heavy chat routes don't steal batch capacity from short prompt routes.


Last quick checklist before running the sync:
- Paste SLO numbers into the top of the doc (done)
- Link INC and Jira keys in Slack thread (linked_artifacts above)
- Have PR links ready for batch cap and autoscaler probe changes
- Set a follow-up Confluence page stub for the runbook and postmortem

End of notes.

-- Erin
(quickfire scribble; will tidy into meeting notes + action tracker after the sync)
